title: Stipend internship that requires buying a "starter kit" vs. stipend internship with a free welcome kit
summary: A coordinator for Vistara Infotech's internship programme messages a student who applied through NaukriHub for a paid digital-marketing internship. In the fraud case, the student must first buy an "internship starter kit" (course access, certificate, ID card) through a purchase link before the offer is confirmed. In the legitimate case, the coordinator confirms the offer, asks for a college NOC and bank details for the stipend, and says the company couriers a welcome kit free of charge.

shared_setting.recipient_profile: an undergraduate student; college and year sampled at generation.
other_facts: Role: remote digital-marketing intern, three months, stipend [AMOUNT_1] (₹5,000–₹15,000 per month).
Both chats mention a "kit", learning material, a certificate on completion, and an ID card.

fraud.label_rationale: The student must buy something from the "employer" before a paid internship is confirmed.
fraud.caller_objective: Sell the worthless kit to as many applicants as possible; there is no internship.
stable_facts: Kit price: [AMOUNT_2] (₹999–₹4,999), "discounted from ₹9,999 for selected interns".
Offer letter is issued "once kit purchase is verified".
Coordinator says the stipend in the first month "covers the kit many times over".

Learning material on the company's learning portal at no cost; a welcome kit (T-shirt, notebook, ID card) couriered free.
Student uploads a college NOC and bank account number + IFSC for the stipend on https://onboard.vistara-infotech.invalid.

cooperative.fraud: Agrees to buy and asks whether UPI works on the link
cooperative.legitimate: Says they will get the NOC from college this week

clarifying.fraud: Asks whether the kit cost can be cut from the stipend
clarifying.legitimate: Asks about working hours and whether the certificate mentions the stipend

resistant.fraud: Says they do not need the course and only want the internship
resistant.legitimate: Says their college will take time to issue the NOC

suspicious.fraud: Says paid internships should not require buying anything
suspicious.legitimate: Asks why bank details are needed and whether it is safe

fraud: coordinator offers a bigger discount and student declines
coordinator says the kit is compulsory and student leaves
legitimate: NOC delayed and coordinator extends the date
coordinator explains account number and IFSC can only be used to send the stipend and no OTP or PIN will be asked.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud coordinator may lower the price or add bonuses ("placement assistance"). They must not switch to OTPs, deposits for tasks, or remote access. The legitimate coordinator must not introduce any purchase or payment after the branch.

must_preserve: role, duration, and stipend identical across cases
_F mandatory kit purchase before offer at turn 7
_L free kit, NOC and stipend bank details only
may_vary: internship area (digital marketing, content writing, HR)
must_not_emit: real e-learning or internship platform names

ambiguities: Kit", "certificate", and "ID card" appear in both cases.
Bank account details appear only in _L; they are not evidence.

Distinct from jr_06: that family gates a full-time offer behind a paid third-party course after an interview; here a student pays the "employer" directly for goods before a stipend internship. Related mechanism; flagged for deduplication review.
Some genuine programmes are unpaid or charge for optional courses sold openly; those belong in jr_15 logic and are not modelled here.

evidence_references.claim: A major IT employer warns that fraudulent agencies charge fees to offer internships or training (CJ03)
The same employer never asks candidates for payment at any stage (CJ01)
Upfront payment is a red flag in fake job schemes (C11)
